metaTitle: Image Dimensions Guide: Width, Height, and Resolution Explained
metaDescription: Learn how image dimensions affect layout, web performance, and print quality, and where resizing fits into a better workflow.

guideContent.section1Title: Why dimensions matter more than raw file size alone
guideContent.section1Body: Image dimensions shape the visual experience and the technical requirements of a file. A banner, a thumbnail, and a product photo each need different dimensions, and resizing to the right size can dramatically improve performance and usability.
guideContent.section2Title: How to choose dimensions with confidence
guideContent.section2Body: The strongest approach is to match dimensions to the real display context, not simply to the largest possible format. This helps reduce unnecessary file weight and keeps the final asset appropriate for the platform.
steps: Start with the platform or layout that will display the image.
Resize to the intended display dimensions rather than the maximum possible size.
Compress after resizing so the file stays practical without losing clarity.

faqs.question: What are image dimensions?
faqs.answer: They are the width and height of the image in pixels, and they directly affect how the file fits a layout or screen.

faqs.question: Does resizing hurt quality?
faqs.answer: It can if you enlarge an image beyond its source quality, but resizing down is often the right and practical choice.

faqs.question: When should I resize before compressing?
faqs.answer: Usually right before compression, because the final pixel dimensions influence how much data the file needs.
